chunks: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from al-Ala' ibn al-Fudayl, who said:

I asked him about a man performing Hajj al-Tamattu' who performed Tawaf, then entered the state of Ihram for Hajj before shortening his hair. He said: 'His Tamattu' is invalidated; it is a Hajj of error.' As for if he entered Ihram forgetfully, then what he did stands and his Tamattu' is complete.

key_terms.أَهَلَّ بِالْحَجِّ: Entered the state of Ihram for Hajj
key_terms.لَبَّى: Entered Ihram (responding to the call of Talbiyah)
key_terms.مُتَمَتِّعٍ: One performing Hajj al-Tamattu' (combining Umrah and Hajj)
key_terms.يُقَصِّرَ: To shorten (hair), a required step in Tamattu'

ai.seo_question: What happens to Hajj al-Tamattu' if the pilgrim enters Ihram for Hajj before shaving their hair?
ai.summary: This narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the critical procedural error in Hajj al-Tamattu' where the pilgrim enters Ihram for Hajj before performing Qasr (hair cutting) after Umrah. The Imam distinguishes between intentional and forgetful actions, ruling that an intentional premature Ihram invalidates the Tamattu' (rendering it a 'Hajj Mabutil' or distinct single Hajj), whereas a forgetful error preserves the validity of the Umrah and allows the Hajj to proceed correctly.
